name: Claude Code 2.1.268 — Gateway Pricing, Plugin --JSON, WebFetch Timeout Fix
hook: Shipped September 10. Adds managed gateway pricing support with `gatewayInternalNetworks` for IPv4 block config, a `--json` flag on all plugin commands (install/uninstall/update/enable/disable), and browser-tab icons for published artifacts. Three high-impact fixes: HTTP 400 failures on third-party Anthropic-compatible endpoints (broken since 2.1.265), WebFetch hanging indefinitely (now aborts at 300s, configurable via `CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_DEADLINE_MS`), and prompt caching silently breaking for SDK sessions using `excludeDynamicSections`. Also resolves high CPU in idle sessions, 'your message came through empty' errors after MCP tool calls, and Slack channel settings lost after workspace moves.

name: Ralph Wiggum Plugin — Official Anthropic Infinite-Loop Plugin, Going Viral
hook: Official plugin inside anthropics/claude-code (145K stars) that creates a persistent AI loop without babysitting: a Stop hook intercepts Claude's exit, feeds the same prompt back, and repeats until a configurable completion-promise string appears. Invented by Geoffrey Huntley ('he just keeps going'), now packaged by Anthropic. Command: `/ralph-loop "Build a REST API" --max-iterations 50 --completion-promise COMPLETE`. Multiple YouTube videos going viral this week. Reddit thread debating it vs the built-in `/loop` — main difference: Ralph runs inside the current session preserving file state across iterations, `/loop` starts fresh each time.

name: zilliztech/claude-context — 12.5K Stars; Semantic Code Search MCP, ~40% Token Cut
hook: 12,500 stars for Zilliz's MCP plugin that replaces directory-load with hybrid BM25 + dense-vector semantic code search. AST-based chunking splits your repo into meaningful units, Merkle-tree incremental sync only re-indexes changed files, and results are retrieved by meaning rather than file-path pattern. Reported ~40% token reduction on large codebases. Supports OpenAI, VoyageAI, Ollama, and Gemini embeddings. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, and 15+ other agents via the MCP protocol.

name: DietrichGebert/ponytail — 128.6K Stars; Laziness Ladder Cuts Code 54–94%
hook: 128,600 stars — up ~24K since last featured August 19. Ponytail enforces a 7-rung laziness ladder before writing a single line of custom code: stdlib first, native platform features, existing dependencies, one-liners, and so on. Benchmarked at ~54% less generated code (range up to 94%), ~20% cheaper API spend, and ~27% faster completions on real FastAPI + React sessions. Targets code bloat; caveman targets prose verbosity — both are complementary.

name: andrej-karpathy-skills — ~209K Stars; Karpathy's Four LLM Coding Rules as a Skill
hook: ~209K stars — the fastest-climbing behavioral skill in the ecosystem. Forrest Chang distilled Andrej Karpathy's January 2026 critique of LLM coding agents into four enforced rules: Think Before Coding, Simplicity First, Surgical Changes, and Goal-Driven Execution. User-reported error rate drop from 41% to 11% in paired testing. Compatible with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode.

name: ECC — Everything Claude Code — 254K Stars; 286 Skills, 68 Agents, Plan Canvas
hook: 254K stars for Affaan Mustafa's agent harness performance system — 10+ months of daily production use crystallized into 286 skills, 68 specialized agents, and 94 commands for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Zed, and others. ECC 2.1 added Plan Canvas (browser-based plan review with annotations), Kimi Code support, and self-hosted compute via Itô GPU marketplace. Hook runtime controls via ECC_HOOK_PROFILE=minimal|standard|strict.

name: JuliusBrussee/caveman — 103.9K Stars; 65% Output Token Cut
hook: 103.9K stars — holding past the 100K milestone. Compresses agent prose into terse caveman-speak while keeping code, commands, and error output byte-perfect. Two independent benchmarks measured 65–75% fewer output tokens with no accuracy loss. v2.5.0 adds `/caveman-compress` for CLAUDE.md and memory files (~46% input token savings on each future session). MIT skill, BSL-1.1 proxy runtime.

name: oh-my-openagent — 68.8K Stars; Ultrawork Token-Maxer Harness
hook: 68.8K stars for the token-focused agent harness: 11 agents, 54+ lifecycle hooks, 5 built-in MCPs, ultrawork mode, and hashline edits. Two editions — Ultimate (Claude Code, OpenCode) and Light (Codex CLI, portable). Creator burned $24K in LLM tokens stress-testing every major agent, then published the config that won.

name: Orca — 62.6K Stars; Fleet Manager for Parallel Coding Agents
hook: 62.6K stars for the ADE (Agent Development Environment) that runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode, and 20+ other agents side-by-side in isolated git worktrees. First commit March 17, 2026 — ~10K stars/month. Desktop app (mac/win/linux), mobile companion (iOS+Android) for steering agents from your phone, SSH remote execution, and integrated terminal splits. MIT.

name: Understand-Anything — 54.7K Stars; Codebase → Interactive Knowledge Graph
hook: 54,700 stars. A multi-agent pipeline scans a repo, extracts every file, function, class, and dependency, and writes a knowledge graph to `.understand-anything/knowledge-graph.json`. An interactive React Flow dashboard renders it with nodes color-coded by layer (API, Service, Data, UI, Utility) and edges showing call paths. The `/understand-chat` command answers natural-language questions about the codebase backed by the graph rather than inline file reads — meaningfully cutting tokens on repo-wide queries. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini CLI.

name: AAS Core (agentic-awesome-skills) — 45.4K Stars; 2,115 Skills With Agent-Owned Selection
hook: 45,400 stars. AAS Core is a local, agent-first control plane: 2,115+ agentic skills indexed in a read-only local MCP catalog. Claude or Codex reads the full catalog via `compose_stack` (a read-only tool), selects exact skill IDs for the current project, and validates the chosen stack before it runs — no ranking, no recommendations, the agent decides. Ships with a CLI, plugin manager, and a browser Workbench for managing installed skill stacks. Compatible with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and more.

name: obsidian-second-brain — 4.4K Stars; Persistent Memory Across 7 CLI Agents
hook: 4,400 stars — up from 1,024 in its first 7 weeks. A cross-CLI skill that wires your Obsidian vault as persistent memory for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Hermes, and Pi. 45 commands: hybrid local+semantic search over vault notes, self-rewriting notes that update after each session, keyless web research (no API key required), `/obsidian-architect` for codebase documentation, and scheduled background agents that maintain the vault while you sleep. Charlie Automates made a dedicated video this week warning devs not to set up a Claude Code second brain without watching it first — this repo was central to that coverage.

name: SEED + PAUL — Claude Code's Plan-First Meta Workflow (Charlie Automates)
hook: PAUL (1.2K stars) is a Plan-Apply-Unify Loop for Claude Code: every task closes with a mandatory UNIFY step that reconciles what was planned vs. what was built, logs decisions, and updates state — designed to prevent the context-rot that degrades quality as sessions grow. SEED (281 stars) is a companion project-incubator: type-aware guided exploration from raw idea to a structured PLANNING.md, then a one-command `/seed launch` hands the plan to PAUL via `paul.toml` frontmatter. Charlie Automates called this combo the 'Claude Code Meta nobody's talking about' in their most recent video. Both are free, MIT-licensed, zero-dependency markdown skills.
